message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact speed right now.  
But you can quickly find out yourself with one of the following methods:

| Method | How to do it |
|--------|--------------|
| **Web‑based speed test** | Open a browser and go to <https://www.speedtest.net> (or <https://fast.com>). Click “Go” and wait for the test to finish. |
| **Command‑line (Windows)** | If you have PowerShell, you can run a quick test with the `Invoke-WebRequest` cmdlet to download a file and time it, but the easiest is to install a dedicated tool. |
| **Command‑line (Linux/macOS)** | Install `speedtest-cli` (`sudo apt install speedtest-cli` on Debian/Ubuntu, `brew install speedtest-cli` on macOS). Then run `speedtest-cli`. |
| **Mobile app** | Download the Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store and run it. |

If you want a quick estimate without installing anything, just use the web site. Once you run the test, you’ll see:

* **Download speed** – how fast data comes into your device (Mbps).
* **Upload speed** – how fast data goes out (Mbps).
* **Ping / latency** – how quickly your device can communicate with the server (ms).

Feel free to share the results if you’d like help interpreting them!
